package_info.package_manager: Linux binary (Mirai-variant botnet, not a traditional package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The Condi botnet is a Mirai-variant DDoS malware that propagates by exploiting router vulnerabilities (notably CVE-2023-1389), kills competing malware and system processes, establishes C2 communication, and launches DDoS attacks. It also hosts and updates its own binaries, and attempts to persist by deleting system shutdown/reboot binaries.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code deletes system binaries responsible for rebooting or shutting down the device, preventing system reboots or shutdowns, which helps the malware persist until a power cycle.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deleting system management binaries is a clear attempt to prevent administrators from easily removing the malware or rebooting the device.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not interfere with core system binaries or prevent system management operations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, embedded systems may remove unused binaries to save space, but not critical system management tools.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Reads /proc/<PID>/status for each running process and compares the Name field to a list of strings (e.g., /bin/busybox, /bin/systemd, /usr/bin, test, /tmp/condi, /tmp/zxcr9999, /var/condibot, etc.), then kills matching processes.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates running processes, checks their names against a blacklist of competing malware and system process names, and kills any matches to eliminate competition and hinder system operation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Killing processes based on name is a common malware technique to remove competitors and evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not indiscriminately kill unrelated processes, especially system or third-party binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security software may terminate known malware, but not in this indiscriminate or self-serving manner.
key_indicators: Targets both malware and system process names

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Kills any process with a binary filename containing architecture-specific extensions (x86, x86_64, arm, arm5, arm6, arm7, mips, mipsel, sh4, ppc).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code scans for processes whose binary filenames contain architecture-specific substrings and kills them, aiming to remove other botnets or malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This is a broad and aggressive method to eliminate competing malware, which can also disrupt legitimate processes.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not kill processes based on architecture-specific substrings in their filenames.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is a malware-specific anti-competition technique.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Generates a random string of at least ten characters from a custom alphanumeric set and attempts to kill any process with this string in its command line.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code generates a random string and attempts to kill any process with this string in its command line, though this is unlikely to match any real process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This appears to be a flawed or incomplete anti-competition feature, possibly intended to target specific malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not kill processes based on random strings.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Generates two random numbers (one between 12 and 32, another between 12 and 20) and kills any process with a command line length matching either number.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code kills any process whose command line length matches randomly generated values, potentially disrupting system operation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This is a highly destructive and indiscriminate technique that can kill legitimate system processes, causing instability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate software kills processes based on command line length.
key_indicators: Kills processes by command line length

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Scans public IPs for open ports 80 or 8080, then sends a hardcoded exploitation request to download and execute a remote shell script from hxxp://cdn2[.]duc3k[.]com/t.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code scans for vulnerable devices, exploits CVE-2023-1389, and downloads/executes a remote shell script to propagate the malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated exploitation and remote code execution for self-propagation is a hallmark of worm/botnet malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not scan the internet for vulnerable devices or execute remote shell scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing tools may perform similar actions, but only with explicit authorization.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Upon receiving a C2 command ([33m\x33\x66\x66[0m), downloads bot binaries from a hardcoded IP and port, then starts a basic HTTP server on a random port above 1024 to host these binaries. Responds to GET/POST/HEAD requests for /arm, /arm7, /mips, /mipsel, /x86_64, /sh4, /ppc, /m68k with the corresponding binaries.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after receiving a C2 command, the code downloads updated malware binaries and hosts them via a local HTTP server, masquerading as Apache, to facilitate further propagation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hosting and serving malware binaries is a core propagation technique for botnets.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not download and serve malware binaries or masquerade as Apache.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software update servers may serve binaries, but not in this context or with this intent.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Implements multiple DDoS attack functions: attack_tcp_syn, attack_tcp_ack, attack_tcp_socket, attack_tcp_thread, attack_tcp_bypass, attack_udp_plain, attack_udp_thread, attack_udp_smart.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after receiving attack commands from C2, the code launches various DDoS attacks (TCP SYN, ACK, UDP floods, etc.) against specified targets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Launching DDoS attacks is inherently malicious and illegal.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate software should launch network floods against arbitrary targets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing tools may simulate DDoS, but only in controlled, authorized environments.

attack_chain.action: Malware is delivered to a vulnerable TP-Link router via exploitation of CVE-2023-1389 (or other vulnerabilities).
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial infection and execution of the malware binary

attack_chain.action: Malware deletes system management binaries to prevent reboot/shutdown and attempts to kill competing malware and system processes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence and exclusive control of the infected device

attack_chain.action: Malware establishes C2 communication and registers itself, awaiting further instructions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ready to receive C2 commands for propagation or attack

attack_chain.action: Upon C2 command, malware downloads updated binaries and starts a local HTTP server to serve them, masquerading as Apache.
attack_chain.leads_to: Facilitates further propagation to new devices

attack_chain.action: Upon C2 command, malware launches DDoS attacks against specified targets using various attack methods.

behavioral_signatures: Deletion of system management binaries (reboot, shutdown, poweroff, halt)
Process killing based on name, filename substring, or command line length
Automated scanning for open HTTP ports (80, 8080) and exploitation attempts
Hosting and serving malware binaries via a local HTTP server masquerading as Apache
Receiving and executing DDoS attack commands from C2
file_indicators: Temporary files or binaries named after architectures (arm, mips, x86, etc.)
network_indicators: C2 protocol traffic with initial bytes \x33\x66\x99
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for deletion or tampering of system management binaries (reboot, shutdown, etc.), unusual process termination activity, and outbound connections to known malicious domains or IPs (cdn2.duc3k.com, 85.217.144.35). Look for local HTTP servers masquerading as Apache on non-standard ports, and detect scanning activity for open HTTP ports. Network monitoring for C2 protocol signatures and DDoS attack traffic can also indicate infection.
